text: x gtable object, object coercible gtable, like ggplot patchwork object. zsort Sort z values? Default FALSE. show_zeroGrobs TRUE/FALSE whether show zeroGrobs. filter character vector regexes, grob names matching least one regex printed. NULL (default), filtering grob name.

title: Print a gtable object as a tibble — gtable_print
text: gtable_print() prints gtable's layout using custom tibble subclass, allowing parts standard printed tibble hidden, like "# tibble..." header line row column types. cells column output slightly different cells column default gtable print method. Specifically, gtable_print() simplifies cells cases grob sits one row one column. E.g., grob just row 3 column 2, default method print "(3-3, 2-2)", gtable_print() prints "(3, 2)".

title: Print a tibble with additional display options — print_tbl
code: x <- tibble::tibble(name = c("Alice", "Bob"), age = c(30, 40)) print_tbl(x) # normal tibble printing #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>   name    age #> * <chr> <dbl> #> 1 Alice    30 #> 2 Bob      40 print_tbl(x, show_types = FALSE)  # drop the row of column types #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>   name  age #> 1 Alice  30 #> 2 Bob    40 print_tbl(x, show_rowid = FALSE)  # drop the column of row IDs #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #> name    age #> <chr> <dbl> #> Alice    30 #> Bob      40 print_tbl(x, show_header = FALSE) # drop the "# A tibble..." line #>   name    age #> * <chr> <dbl> #> 1 Alice    30 #> 2 Bob      40
